description: Five representative transactions evaluated against the canonical governance manifest. One commits; four are refused at the write path. Each is traceable to a row in /data. Outcomes illustrate the enforcement model, not a specific product build.

transactions.label: Valid Requested Ship Date change
transactions.why_a_passive_database_would_accept_it: It is a well-formed update; a passive store would accept it regardless of the approval.
transactions.why_an_application_layer_workflow_might_: N/A — this transaction is valid and should commit. It is included as the control case.

transactions.label: Invalid change with ambiguous approval

approval_artifact.snippet: We have some flexibility on the August deliveries if it helps you.

transactions.why_a_passive_database_would_accept_it: The row is syntactically valid and an approval_ref string is present; the store has no notion of whether the reference authorizes the change.
transactions.why_an_application_layer_workflow_might_: The workflow checks that an approval reference is attached, not that the referenced artifact names this order, this field, and these two values. Presence of a reference is mistaken for consent.

transactions.label: Invalid change through Expected Ship Date substitution
transactions.why_a_passive_database_would_accept_it: expected_ship_date is just a column; a passive store updates it on request with no concept of commitment semantics.
transactions.why_an_application_layer_workflow_might_: The approval control is attached to the requested_ship_date screen. This update targets a different field over the API and never reaches that screen, so no control is invoked. This is the decisive move in the failure chain.

transactions.label: Invalid supplier alias receipt
transactions.why_a_passive_database_would_accept_it: supplier_reference is free text; the store writes the string and does not require it to resolve to a canonical vendor.
transactions.why_an_application_layer_workflow_might_: The receiving screen accepts a typed supplier name and, at most, checks it is non-empty. It does not require the name to resolve to a single approved canonical supplier, so an unmapped alias becomes supplier-of-record and poisons downstream traceability.

transactions.label: Invalid agent-generated update optimizing on-time metric
transactions.why_a_passive_database_would_accept_it: The agent issues a syntactically valid update to a date column; the store commits it. The agent's objective is invisible to the database.
transactions.why_an_application_layer_workflow_might_: A prompt filter or agent wrapper governs what the agent is asked to do, not what the substrate accepts. The agent reaches a legitimate endpoint that lacks the commitment invariant, so no wrapper is in the write path to stop it. Governance must live where state is committed, not around the agent.
